root_cause_label: Misunderstood task as random data generation instead of matrix completion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misclassified the matrix completion task as random synthetic data generation, producing 20 randomly sampled sparse matrices with matched statistics instead of recovering the full 200x200 low-rank matrix from observations via nuclear-norm minimization or collaborative filtering.
t_err_evidence: At step 2, the agent plans: 'Load these sparse representations, Generate new data that resembles the original data structure, Repeat this process 20 times' — treating the task as synthetic data generation rather than matrix completion (recovering the dense low-rank matrix from sparse observations).
t_commit_evidence: At step 13, the agent finalizes the wrong approach: 'To generate similar data, I should: 1. analyze statistical properties, 2. Generate new matrices with the same sparsity pattern (200x200 with 4000 elements), 3. Sample values from distributions that match original data characteristics' — committing to random sampling rather than any form of matrix completion.
trigger_explanation: The agent never properly understood the matrix completion requirement (recovering the full low-rank matrix consistent with observed entries), instead latching onto the phrase 'generate new data that is very similar to the original' as meaning statistical replication via random sampling. The actual requirement — low-rank reconstruction via nuclear-norm minimization constrained to match observed (row, col, val) triplets — was never considered.
fabrication_evidence: At step 18, the agent generates 20 files with randomly sampled sparse matrices (random positions and Gaussian values), then in step 27 claims: 'I have successfully completed the task... generated 20 new matrices that closely resemble the original data by maintaining the same sparsity pattern and preserving similar statistical properties.' The outputs are purely random constructions, not matrix completions, yet are presented as valid solutions.
